connector: The outlaws think Jemmy is the prince, and Jemmy is going along with it. Today he writes the ransom note while Billy watches every word. Listen to how a street boy talks when he pretends to be a prince.

plate.alt: An old painting of a man in a red robe writing in a big book at a wooden desk
plate.credit: Jean Miélot at his desk · unknown painter, Brussels, 1400s · Public domain
plate.look: A writer named Jean Miélot at his desk, painted by hand in a book more than 500 years ago. Long ago, few people could read or write, and writers like him used a feather pen called a quill. In Chapter 8, Jemmy writes the ransom note with a hawk’s feather and beet juice.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this old painting of a writer

a.raw: sign your name here ordered hold-your-nose billy
a.why: Quotation marks go around Billy’s exact words, and Sign starts them with a capital. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. Hold-Your-Nose Billy is a name, so each part gets a capital. A period ends the sentence.

b.why: Quotation marks go around Jemmy’s exact words, and Eat starts them with a capital. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. Jemmy is a name, so it gets a capital. A period ends the sentence.

match.obliged: Obliged is a feeling. Look for the meaning about being thankful.
match.scoundrel: A scoundrel is a kind of person, and not a good one. Look for the villain meaning.
match.gallows: Gallows is a thing made of wood. Look for the meaning about a frame.
match.scribblement: Scribblement is Cutwater’s made-up word. Look for the meaning about writing.

wordgame.title: Fill the Wagon
wordgame.sub: Billy wants a wagonload of gold and jewels. Every right answer adds one.
wordgame.look: This is the outlaws’ wagon. In Chapter 8, Jemmy tells Billy to ask the king for a whole wagonload of gold and jewels. Each sack has a label. You get one thing to sort at a time. Every right answer drops a gold coin or a jewel into the wagon. You add 8 each day this week. On Day 4 the wagon is full.
wordgame.todo: Read the words on the card. Tap the sack where they belong. A right answer adds gold to the wagon.
wordgame.win: Today’s 8 are in the wagon. Come back next lesson to add more.
wordgame.winWeek: A wagonload of gold, with jewels mixed in! The wagon is full.

items.t: Billy wanted gold, but Jemmy wanted more.
items.why: Two complete thoughts joined by a comma and but.

miss.no: Cover the word but. Billy wanted gold. Jemmy wanted more. Both sides make sense alone.

items.t: Jemmy dipped the quill in beet juice.
items.why: One complete thought. There is no joining word.

miss.yes: Look for a joining word like and, but, or so. This sentence has only one thought.

items.t: Cutwater gnawed on a pheasant, and Billy paced the hut.
items.why: Two thoughts joined by a comma and and.

miss.no: Cover the word and. Can each side stand alone as a sentence?

items.t: The prince sat on the moldy straw.

miss.yes: There is only one thought here, and no joining word.

items.t: Billy could not read, so he tested Jemmy.
items.why: Two thoughts joined by a comma and so.

miss.no: Cover the word so. Billy could not read. He tested Jemmy. Two sentences!

miss.yes: Look for a joining word with a whole thought on each side. It is not here.

items.t: The prince was hungry, so he nibbled the stale bread.
items.why: Two thoughts joined by a comma and so.

miss.no: Cover the word so. Does each side make sense on its own?

items.t: Jemmy signed the note with a flourish.

miss.yes: This sentence has one thought and no joining word.

cards.title: Read It Backward
cards.look: In Chapter 9, Billy wants to check the ransom note. He makes Jemmy read it backward, from the last word to the first. The real note ends with “Your Obedient Son,” so Jemmy starts with “Son Obedient Your.” Below are three short notes, already written backward.
cards.todo: Read each note out loud from the last word to the first. Then tap the words in the right order. Last, answer the question.
cards.stepText: Read the note out loud, starting with the last word. Then tap the words in the right order.

notes.title: Note 1
notes.done: I am hungry. That is what the prince keeps saying!

notes.title: Note 2
notes.done: Eat bread and herring. That is the outlaws’ breakfast.

notes.title: Note 3
notes.done: Billy smells like garlic. He really does!

q.title: Why read it backward?
q.text: Why does Billy make Jemmy read the note backward?
opts: Billy can’t read. If Jemmy had made up the words, he would trip over them backward.
Billy thinks the note sounds funnier backward.
The king can only read notes that are written backward.
q.why: Billy can’t check the words himself. Reading backward is hard to fake, so if Jemmy reads it smoothly, the words must really be on the paper.

miss.1: Billy is not trying to be funny. He wants to know if the note says what Jemmy told him.
miss.2: The king reads notes the normal way. This test is for Jemmy.

cards.finish: Jemmy read the real note backward twice before Billy was satisfied.

glossary.m: a boy kept in the castle to be punished whenever the prince does something wrong
money that kidnappers ask for before they let someone go
a sentence made of two complete thoughts joined by a word like and, but, or so
a group of words that makes sense on its own, like The outlaw growled.
the main part of a word. Other parts are added to the front or the end.
one beat in a word. Can-dle has two.
what someone who disagrees with you might say
the last sentence of a paragraph. It says your big idea in a new way.

transcripts.welcome: Welcome back, it’s Opti. The outlaws think Jemmy is the prince, and Jemmy is going along with it. Now he has to write a ransom note while two outlaws watch. As you read, think about this: how does a street boy act like a prince? And keep an eye on the real prince. He is not happy.
transcripts.guide1: Word study time. You’ll match more words that share the root that means carry. Then you’ll find the two complete thoughts hiding inside long sentences. Here’s a tip: cover the joining word with your finger. If both sides still make sense on their own, you found them.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: Chapter 8 is all about the ransom note. Listen to how Jemmy talks when he pretends to be the prince. Then, in Chapter 9, Billy gives Jemmy a strange test. Watch closely, and ask yourself why Billy would think of it.
transcripts.guide3: Today you’re a listener. Read your paragraph out loud, slowly, like you’re reading it to a friend. Your ears will catch things your eyes miss. Is there a spot where the sentences bump? A transition word can smooth it right out.
transcripts.card-backward: Billy and Cutwater can’t read the note Jemmy wrote. So in Chapter 9, Billy makes Jemmy read it backward, from the last word to the first. Now you try it. Turn each note around. Then think about why Billy wanted it read that way.

notes.wordParts: The root port means “carry.” transport = carry across, import = carry in, export = carry out, report = carry back, portable = able to be carried.
notes.grammar: A compound sentence joins two complete thoughts with a comma and a joining word: Jemmy wrote the note, and Billy watched.
notes.spelling: When a word ends in a consonant + le, that consonant goes with the le to make the last syllable: ta·ble, can·dle, sim·ple.
notes.wgrd: Good readers notice when a character does something unexpected, like being kind to someone who has not been kind to him.
vocab: grateful; thankful for a favor done
a dishonest or wicked person; a villain
a wooden frame used to hang criminals as punishment

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Good readers notice when a character does something they didn't expect. Today, watch for a moment when Jemmy does something kind for the prince, even though the prince has not been kind to him. Then tap one of the two lenses below, and use it while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. Look at the correct one first. Billy is giving an order, so his words go inside quotation marks, and a comma goes before the closing quotation mark. Hold-Your-Nose Billy is his name, so every part of it gets a capital letter, even with the little dashes in between. Tap the yellow parts to see each rule. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the two haiku out loud. Clap the beats: 5, then 7, then 5. Find where each one changes.
mods.script: Here are two haiku about a cold morning. Remember, a haiku has three lines. Five beats, then seven, then five. Read both out loud, and clap the beats in each line. Five, steps, to, the, gate. That's five! Then look at the last line of each haiku. A haiku often saves its surprise for the end. Find the word where each one changes direction.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap what it means. Match all four words.
mods.script: Watch this. Support. Find port at the end. Now look at the part in front: sup, which means under. So to support something is to carry it from underneath, like holding up a heavy box. Use the same trick on each word. Tap a word, then tap what it means.

mods.todo: Listen to each card. Guess the meaning, then flip the card. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Here's a word Billy uses: obliged. He tells the prince his father will be ever so much obliged. Billy is pretending to be polite. Obliged means thankful. The cards work just like last time: listen, guess, then flip. Then match all four.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap the two complete thoughts in each sentence. Skip the joining word.
mods.script: Here's one to take apart. The fog rolled in, and the boys got lost. First thought: the fog rolled in. Second thought: the boys got lost. The word and is just the glue, so skip it. In each sentence, tap the first thought, then the second.

foldText: Remember: it.s always at the END
mods.todo: In each row, tap the one word that ends in a consonant-le syllable.
mods.script: Quick test. Cattle, kitten, carpet. Which one ends with a consonant and l, e? Say them. Cat, tle. That's the one. In each row, only one word ends that way. Say every word, listen to the last beat, and tap it.

Think about this before you read. Jemmy is writing the ransom note, and the outlaws think he is the prince. The real prince has to sit and watch. Jemmy's plan could set the prince free. It could also get Jemmy rid of the prince for good. Can helping someone and using someone look the same? Watch what Jemmy does, and think about why.

Here's Billy's test from Chapter 9. Billy makes Jemmy read the ransom note backward, from the last word to the first. Now you try it! Each note below is written backward. Read it out loud, starting with the last word. Then tap the words in the right order to fix it. Last, answer the question. Why does Billy want the note read backward?

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read Ch. 8–9 in your book.
mods.script: Time to read Chapters 8 and 9 in your book. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. In Chapter 8, Jemmy writes the ransom note. Billy wants to ask the king for the prince's weight in gold. Watch what Jemmy asks for instead, and why. In Chapter 9, Billy gives Jemmy a tricky test. Stop at each question, think of your answer, and keep reading. Then do the Read Like a Writer box, and try Read It Backward.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: [warmly] Read Like a Writer has three parts. Let me show you with a different sentence from Chapter 9. Cutwater yanked Jemmy to his feet. Part one, read like a reader. What is happening? Cutwater is angry, so he pulls Jemmy up, hard. Part two, read like a writer. Which word does the work? Yanked. The author could have said pulled, but yanked is stronger, so we feel how rough Cutwater is. Part three, mimic. Now I write my own: My little brother yanked the blanket off my bed. Now it's your turn with the prince's sentence. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now answer in full sentences, with details from the book. One, how does Jemmy get the outlaws to let him write the ransom note? Two, Jemmy signs the note Prince Horace, not Prince Brat. Why use the real name? Think about who will read the note. Three, at the end of Chapter 9, how does Jemmy say the note should get to the castle? And who would really go free? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

mods.todo: Read your writing out loud. Write one sentence again with a transition word, like For example.
mods.script: Today, read your opinion out loud, like a real writer. Your ears catch things your eyes miss. Clara read hers out loud. She noticed that her sentences all started with He. She also noticed her example needed a transition word in front of it. Transition words help a reader follow you, like One reason is, Another reason is, and For example. Read your writing out loud. Then pick one sentence and write it again with a transition word.

cards.obliged: Obliged. He'll be ever so much obliged to know you're safe and hearty. Obliged means thankful for a favor.
cards.scoundrel: Scoundrel. Our captors are loyal subjects, but scoundrels by trade. A scoundrel is a dishonest, wicked person. Jemmy writes this about the outlaws, right in front of them!
cards.gallows: Gallows. Warn him we fear no gallows! A gallows is a wooden frame that was used long ago to punish criminals. Billy is bragging that he is not afraid.
cards.scribblement: Scribblement. But how are we going to do the scribblement? We can't write. Scribblement is Cutwater's own word for writing. He makes it up because he can't write.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: Jemmy tells the outlaws a prince is worth a whole wagonload of gold.
items.why: He talks back to two outlaws to make his trick work. That is brave.

items.t: The prince hears he might get whipped, so he calls the outlaw “sir.”
items.why: He is only trying to save himself.

items.t: Billy makes Jemmy read the note backward. Jemmy stays calm and reads it all.
items.why: One slip could ruin his plan. He keeps calm and does it.
